title: 3R-Adapter: Retrieval, Rewiring, and Refinement for Efficient Adaptation of 3D Reconstruction Model
claim: Foundation models thrive on abundant data but fail in data-scarce domains; channel-wise adapters can't model correspondence, ours adapts relations explicitly.
layout: 2 panels; (a) bar chart with pipeline inset, (b) stacked prior vs ours columns
description: Panel (a) is a large log-scale bar chart of dataset sizes. Blue bars for large pre-training datasets (DL3DV, ScanNet and others) decline from left to right. A pink shaded region at right holds much shorter red bars for long-tail datasets, under the red text 'Data Scaling Fails Here: High Cost of 3D Ground Truth'. Above the bars, a small diagram shows a flame-marked '3R Model' pre-trained on scene reconstruction. A frozen (snowflake) 3R Model with a PEFT module then adapts to three thumbnails: low-light, human-scene and test-time adaptation. Panel (b) has two columns separated by dashed lines. On the left, LoRA (Down/Up) and Adapter (MLP) are labeled 'channel-wise adjustment without correspondence adaptation'. On the right, 3R-Adapter flows from Self-Proj. and Ref.-Proj. through retrieval, sampling offsets and weights, rewiring, and consistency refinement. A blue caption reads 'correspondence-aware adaptation'.
caption: The data scaling bottleneck in 3D pre-training and our relational adaptation paradigm. (a) While foundation models thrive on massive data, they struggle to generalize to long-tail 3D domains due to the high cost of dense 3D ground truth. (b) Conventional PEFT methods (e.g., LoRA, Adapter) rely on implicit, channel-wise feature adjustment, which struggle to model the correspondence relationship in data-scarce scenarios. In contrast, our 3R-Adapter shifts the paradigm to explicit relational adaptation via Deformable Retrieval, Relational Rewiring, and Consistency Refinement, effectively establishing robust cross-view correspondences without destroying pre-trained priors.
abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models have demonstrated strong generalization under large-scale pre-training, yet they struggle in long-tail scenarios such as low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation. We observe relational attention structure collapse, manifested as the failure of cross-view correspondences, as a primary cause of these limitations. While adaptation offers a practical way to bridge this gap, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches mainly perform channel-wise feature adjustment and lack mechanisms to explicitly adapt relational structures, leaving correspondence failures unresolved. In this work, we formulate adaptation of 3D reconstruction models as a problem of correspondence recovery under domain shift and propose 3R-Adapter, a PEFT paradigm for long-tail 3D reconstruction scenarios. Our method consists of three components: Deformable Retrieval for task-adaptive relation candidate retrieval, Relational Rewiring for reconstructing cross-view relational structures, and Consistency Refinement for injecting the rewired relations into stable predictions. Extensive experiments on low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation demonstrate that our approach significantly improves robustness over existing PEFT methods while maintaining efficient lightweight adaptation. Our code is released at https://github.com/PKU-OV3-LAB/3R-Adapter.
